summary: Release-pipeline-only change to .github/workflows/release.yml plus two new node scripts. (1) The `release` job now waits, before `changeset publish`, until npm lists every native package that publish-ffi/publish-auth just published; this fails closed on timeout. (2) The production EQL asset jobs (eql-sql, eql-docs, eql-image) are now driven by a new `eql-assets` job that runs on every production push whatever `release` did, and decides from npm, the `eql-<version>` tag and this run's publishedPackages, building at the commit the `@cipherstash/eql@<version>` tag names. (3) The EQL jobs use `!cancelled()` plus explicit result checks instead of the implicit success(). No library code, payload or SQL changes. Because EQL is armed at head (FROZEN_PUBLISHERS is empty), merging is itself expected to create the eql-3.0.6 tag and GitHub release and dispatch an image build that moves `postgres-eql:latest` — an outward, hard-to-reverse action. The main residual risks are that the decision keys only on the eql tag, so a partly built asset set (SQL done, docs/image failed, e.g. the GHCR write access AGENTS.md still lists as open) is treated as complete on later pushes, and that the failed-publish recovery path relies on unverified changesets/action behaviour (outputs and tags on failure). Both fail loudly or leave a gap rather than shipping wrong bytes. Script tests and actionlint passed in CI, but they model GitHub semantics rather than observe them.

behaviour_changes.description: publish-ffi and publish-auth export a `published` output (space-separated name@version list, including versions skipped as already published). The `release` job runs scripts/wait-for-npm-versions.mjs before changesets/action, polling `npm view <name> versions` every 15s for up to 900s; registry errors are retried; timeout fails the step before `changeset publish`. Empty lists return immediately.

The `release` job no longer computes eql_published/eql_version/eql_prerelease; it exports changesets' publishedPackages directly. A new `eql-assets` job (needs classify, gate, release; `!cancelled()`, production, gate success) runs on every production run, regardless of the `release` result, and decides needed/version/prerelease/ref.

EQL asset decision changes from 'this run published EQL' to 'armed AND no eql-<version> tag AND (npm lists the tree version OR this run published it)'. Assets are built at the commit named by the @cipherstash/eql@<version> tag (or the run's sha if this run published and no tag exists); otherwise the job throws. This enables automatic repair of releases on later pushes — starting with EQL 3.0.6 on the merge of this PR (tag, GitHub release, image with floating tags).

eql-sql/eql-docs/eql-image conditions start with `!cancelled()` and name required upstream results (eql-sql success for docs; eql-sql and eql-docs success for image) instead of the implicit success(), so they run when publish-ffi/publish-auth were skipped or `release` failed.
GitHub expression evaluator moved to scripts/__tests__/lib/expressions.mjs and extended with cancelled(); new job-graph and process tests for both scripts.

failure_scenarios.title: A partly built EQL asset set is treated as complete by every later run
failure_scenarios.trigger: eql-sql succeeds (creating tag eql-<v> and the GitHub release) but eql-docs or eql-image fails — e.g. the image push fails because write access to ghcr.io/cipherstash/postgres-eql from this repo is still missing (AGENTS.md lists it as an open cutover step). Likely on the very first run after merge for 3.0.6.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: eqlAssets() returns needed=false as soon as tagCommit('eql-<v>') finds the tag (eql-release-assets.mjs:86-89); it never checks for the docs bundle or the image. eql-image additionally requires eql-docs success.
failure_scenarios.consequence: SQL release eql-3.0.6 exists while docs bundle and/or postgres-eql:3.0.6/:latest do not; later pushes report 'nothing owed' and never repair it. postgres-eql:latest keeps serving 3.0.5 SQL while npm and the GitHub release say 3.0.6 — a version skew between the client package and the SQL bundle customers get from the image. Recoverable by re-running failed jobs in that run or a manual dispatch.

failure_scenarios.title: Failed-publish recovery depends on unverified changesets/action behaviour and may fail every push to main
failure_scenarios.trigger: `changeset publish` publishes @cipherstash/eql then fails on another package (the E402 case), and changesets/action does not set publishedPackages and/or does not push the @cipherstash/eql@<v> tag when the publish command exits non-zero.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: eql-assets reads PUBLISHED_PACKAGES straight from steps.changesets.outputs.publishedPackages (release.yml:509) on the assumption that the action sets it on failure; if empty and npm already lists the version with no changesets tag, eqlAssets() throws (eql-release-assets.mjs:98-106). eql-assets runs on every production push (release.yml:669-676).
failure_scenarios.consequence: eql-assets fails on every subsequent push to main (red release workflow) until someone pushes the tag or builds the assets by hand; assets missing in the meantime. Fails closed — no wrong bytes are built.

failure_scenarios.title: Wait passes but changeset publish still sees a stale npm packument and fails with E402
failure_scenarios.trigger: npm registry/CDN eventual consistency: `npm view <name> versions` returns the new version, then changesets' own `npm info` lookup hits a stale cached packument.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The wait (wait-for-npm-versions.mjs:63-90) checks once per package and stops polling as soon as it is listed; changesets performs a separate lookup afterwards with no guarantee of the same view.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Same failure as before the change: release job fails with E402, other JS packages may already be published; re-run needed. Loud, recoverable.

recommended_controls.description: Treat merging as an EQL 3.0.6 release action: before merge confirm the @cipherstash/eql@3.0.6 tag points at 23e9af3f, that this repo can push to ghcr.io/cipherstash/postgres-eql, and that moving :latest to 3.0.6 is intended.

Watch the first post-merge Release JS run: eql-assets reports needed=true ref=23e9af3f; eql-3.0.6 release has SQL and docs bundles; image workflow pushes <pg>-3.0.6 and moves :latest. If any downstream EQL job fails, re-run failed jobs in that same run (later pushes will not repair it).
Confirm from changesets/action v1.9.0 source that publishedPackages is set and tags are pushed (commitMode github-api) when `changeset publish` exits non-zero.

Document recovery: for a stuck eql-assets failure push the @cipherstash/eql@<v> tag at the publishing commit; for a partial asset set dispatch _build-eql-docs / release-postgres-eql-image manually. A wrongly created eql-<v> release/tag can be deleted, but moved image floating tags must be re-pointed.
On the next release that includes protect-ffi or auth, check the wait step log and that changeset publish no longer hits E402.
